The study included 99 patients with prostate cancer who underwent salvage radiotherapy.
The median follow-up time for the patients was 29 months.
The primary endpoint of the study was biochemical recurrence-free survival (BRFS).
The radiomic signature achieved a C-index of 0.71.
The radiomic signature outperformed clinical models in predicting biochemical recurrence.
The most predictive radiomic feature was mean intensity.
The study used PSMA-PET-guided CT imaging.
The patients were stratified into low- or high-probability groups based on predictions of the radiomic signature.
The radiomic signature achieved an AUC of 0.73 at 24 months follow-up.
The combined clinical-radiomic signature achieved an AUC of 0.63 at 24 months follow-up.
The radiomic signature had the highest clinical net benefit compared to the two alternative signatures.
The study used a nested cross-validation approach to evaluate the performance of the radiomic signature.
The radiomic signature was developed using a recently published approach.
The study used a total of 104 radiomic features.
The radiomic signature was evaluated using time-dependent receiver-operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis.
